theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A manufacturing firm in Kingston set a five-year strategy two years ago. Why should its managers monitor and review the strategic direction regularly, rather than wait for year five?
options: To catch changes early and adjust while there is time
To give the board a reason to replace the managers often
To avoid having to set any targets for the next few years
To prove that the original plan was right in every detail

questions.stem: A distributor of building materials in Montego Bay wants to scan its external environment. Which tool groups the factors as political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental?
options: SWOT analysis
Gantt chart
PESTLE analysis
Fishbone diagram

questions.stem: Interest rates on consumer loans in Jamaica rise sharply. For a furniture retailer whose strategy depends on customers buying on credit, what does this signal?
options: Credit sales will probably rise quickly next year
Customers may borrow less, so credit sales may slow
The retailer's suppliers will have to cut their prices
The retailer no longer needs to track its credit sales

questions.stem: A courier company's strategic objective is to be the most reliable delivery service in the Corporate Area. Which key performance indicator (KPI) best tracks progress toward it?
options: Number of vans painted in the new company colours
Number of staff who attended the annual staff party
Total fuel bought by the company each month
Percentage of parcels delivered on the promised day

questions.stem: Which of these is a leading indicator for a hotel group's goal of more repeat bookings?
options: Last year's total repeat bookings for the group
The profit reported in the annual accounts
Guest satisfaction scores collected at checkout
The number of rooms sold over the last year

questions.stem: A firm's strategy targets 2,400 new business customers by the end of the year. At the end of the third quarter it has 1,500. What percentage of the yearly target has it reached?
Halfway through the year, a security company has reached only 35% of its yearly sales target. The manager learns that a new rival is undercutting its prices. What should the manager do first?
options: Lower the target to 35% so that the result looks better
Cut prices below the rival's at once on every contract
Wait until the end of the year before taking any action
Analyse the cause and the options, then propose a response

questions.stem: For several years a well-known Jamaican retailer kept the same approach while its customers moved to online shopping, and its sales slowly fell. What is this called?
options: Strategic alignment
Strategic drift
Market penetration
Vertical integration

questions.stem: When should a company review whether its mission statement still fits?
options: Only when the company changes its logo or its colours
When major changes in its market or purpose occur
Every week, at the regular meeting of supervisors
Never, because a mission must stay the same forever

questions.stem: In a balanced scorecard, under which perspective would a manager place 'training hours per employee'?
options: Financial
Customer
Internal business process
Learning and growth

questions.stem: A financial institution in Jamaica is reviewing its strategy. Why should it gather views from customers, staff and regulators?
options: They see risks and needs that managers may miss
They can then be blamed if the strategy fails
They will want to take over the planning work
It removes any need to look at the figures

questions.stem: A review finds that a new highway will cut the travel time from a firm's Kingston factory to its main market in Ocho Rios. In a SWOT analysis, where does this belong?
options: Strength
Weakness
Opportunity
Threat

questions.stem: A tourism company is unsure whether visitor arrivals will rise, stay flat or fall over the next three years. Which approach helps it test its strategy against each of these futures?
options: Cost-plus pricing
Job evaluation
Stock rotation
Scenario planning

questions.stem: Before using the monthly figures sent in by branch managers to review the strategy, what should the strategy manager check?
options: That each branch used its own definitions and dates
That the data are accurate, complete and comparable
That the figures show the results the board hopes for
That the reports are long enough to look thorough

questions.stem: The board of a distribution company has changed one of its strategic objectives. What should managers do next?
options: Keep the change quiet until the next annual report
Tell only the senior team and leave the others guessing
Explain the change and update the unit plans
Ask each unit to carry on with its old plan unchanged

questions.stem: A firm's revenue rose from J$480 million to J$540 million in a year. What was the growth rate?
A juice maker had sales of J$900 million in a market worth J$6 billion. What is its market share?
A rival opens three stores near a hardware chain's branches in St Ann. What is the best first step in the chain's strategy review?
options: Copy every price the rival advertises in the newspaper
Ignore the rival until its stores have closed down
Ask staff to say bad things about the rival's stores
Assess the rival's offer and its likely effect on sales

questions.stem: A manager is preparing a quarterly strategy report for the board. What should it focus on?
options: A full list of every task that each department completed
The manager's personal views about the other managers
Progress on objectives, key risks and decisions needed
Pictures from the staff sports day and social events

questions.stem: Which is the best way to manage the risks to a firm's strategic objectives?
options: Leave risk for the insurance company to worry about
Keep a strategic risk register with owners and reviews
Assume each risk will be handled when it comes up later
List the risks once at the start and never look again

questions.stem: During a strategic review, a manager at a Spanish Town company carries out a gap analysis. What two things is she comparing?
options: Last year's prices with this year's prices
Each staff member's pay with the average market rate
Where the business is now and where it aims to be
The space between two buildings on the site

questions.stem: A Kingston software firm finds that a small side service, data backup, is growing much faster than its main products. How should the strategy review treat this?
options: Stop the service, since it was not part of the plan
Assess it as a possible new direction to support
Hide the results so the original plan looks right
Leave it alone and never mention it to the board

questions.stem: A review shows that 70% of a firm's marketing budget still goes to a product line that the new strategy plans to phase out. What should the manager recommend?
options: Move resources toward the priorities in the strategy
Increase the budget for the product being phased out
Keep the budget as it is, since it was agreed last year
Split the budget equally across all the product lines

questions.stem: Which review timetable best suits a firm's five-year strategic plan?
options: Look at the plan only when a crisis happens
Review it once, at the end of the five years
Check it daily and change it whenever sales dip
Track KPIs monthly and review the plan yearly

questions.stem: A hotel compares its staff turnover and guest scores with those of the best hotels in the Caribbean. What is this called?
options: Brainstorming
Forecasting
Downsizing
Benchmarking

questions.stem: A review finds that branch managers do not understand how their targets link to the company's strategy. What is the most likely result?
options: Effort that does not support the strategic objectives
A steady rise in the company's market share each year
Lower costs for the company's head office team
Faster approval of the company's capital budget

questions.stem: A review shows that a firm's export strategy is failing because shipping costs have risen. Before recommending a change of direction, what should the manager do?
options: Announce the new direction to the media straight away
Test the options against data, costs, risks and capability
Drop exports at once without telling the board first
Choose whichever option the most senior manager prefers

questions.stem: Which source gives the most reliable picture of how customers see a firm's drive to improve service?
options: A few comments the manager heard at a party
The views of the firm's own sales staff only
A properly sampled customer survey over time
One angry post on social media last week

questions.stem: A new data protection law is coming into force. How should a firm that sells online respond in its strategic review?
options: Treat it as a minor matter for the IT clerk alone
Assess its effect on plans, systems and costs
Ignore it until a customer complains about data
Stop all online sales until the law is repealed

questions.stem: Which action best shows that a firm's operational plans are aligned with its strategy?
options: Each unit writes its plan without seeing the strategy
Units copy last year's plans and change the dates
Each unit's targets link to a strategic objective
Each unit sets targets that are easy to reach

questions.stem: Mobile payments are growing fast in Jamaica, but a small chain of pharmacies has no plan for them. In a PESTLE review, which factor is this?
options: Political
Legal
Environmental
Technological

questions.stem: A strategy dashboard has 60 indicators, and the board says it cannot see what matters. What should the manager do?
options: Pick a few key indicators linked to each objective
Add even more indicators so that nothing is left out
Remove the dashboard and report only in words
Change the colours so the dashboard looks better

questions.stem: A firm cut its prices six months ago to win back market share. How should the manager judge whether this worked?
options: Compare share, volume and margin with the targets
Ask the sales team whether they personally liked the change
Check whether the rival has complained about it
Count how many adverts mentioned the new prices

questions.stem: An industry analysis shows that buyers have strong bargaining power. What does this mean for a supplier's strategy?
options: It can raise prices freely without losing any sales
Customers can push prices down or switch easily
There are no rival firms in the industry at all
New firms find it impossible to enter the market

questions.stem: A review of a mining firm's strategy finds strong profits but rising complaints from nearby communities. Why should this matter to the strategic direction?
options: Complaints only matter when they appear in the national press
Community views have no link to a firm's long-term results
Profits always outweigh any concern raised by neighbours
Loss of trust can threaten its licence to operate and growth

questions.stem: When a firm's strategy was set, it assumed that the exchange rate would stay stable. Why should a review check this assumption?
options: Exchange rates never affect a Jamaican business
Only the finance clerk needs to know the rate
If it has changed, costs and prices may be wrong
The assumption was approved, so it cannot change

questions.stem: In a strategy review report, what should support each recommendation?
options: The writer's personal feelings about each department
A promise that there will be no risks at all
Evidence, the expected benefits and the risks
The number of pages in the full report

questions.stem: A review asks what a firm does better than its rivals that customers value and rivals find hard to copy. What is this?
options: A fixed cost
A sunk cost
A short-term liability
A core competence

questions.stem: Why should a manager involve team leaders in reviewing how the strategy is working on the ground?
options: So they can take the blame if the targets are missed
They see problems early and help make changes work
So the manager can avoid making any decisions personally
So the board does not need to approve any changes

questions.stem: A firm's strategy relies on one overseas supplier for its main raw material. What should the review recommend?
options: Develop other suppliers or plans in case of disruption
Sign a ten-year deal with the same single supplier
Stop tracking the supplier's delivery times and quality
Assume shipping will always arrive on time

questions.stem: Which question belongs in a strategic review rather than in routine monthly budget control?
options: Was the stationery bill higher than budget last month?
Did the cleaner work every one of the hours on the roster?
Was petty cash counted at the end of each week?
Are we still in the right markets with the right products?

questions.stem: Which is NOT a sign that a firm's strategic direction needs review?
options: A large new competitor enters the local market
Key customers change how they buy
The office is repainted in the usual colours
A new law changes how the firm may operate

questions.stem: A firm's net profit fell from J$60 million to J$45 million while revenue stayed at J$500 million. By how many percentage points did the net profit margin fall?
options: 3 points
15 points
25 points
9 points

questions.stem: A manager must present a strategy review to the board in 15 minutes. What is the best approach?
options: Read out every table in the 40-page report in order
Lead with key findings and the decisions needed
Show only good news so that the board stays positive
Spend most of the time on the history of the company

questions.stem: After an annual strategy review, what should a firm do with the lessons learned?
options: Record them and use them in the next planning cycle
File them in a cabinet where no one will ever read them
Share them only with the managing director

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What four-letter abbreviation names the tool that sets out an organisation's strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats?
What three-letter abbreviation names a measure chosen to track progress toward a key objective?
A firm set a target of 500 new contracts for the year and won 420. What percentage of the target did it achieve?
What two-word name is given to the performance framework that measures financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth results?
What term describes an indicator that measures results already achieved, such as last year's profit?
A company's revenue grew from J$250 million to J$300 million in one year. What was the percentage growth?
What word names a company's statement of what it wants to become in the long term?
Porter's model of the pressures in an industry counts rivals, new entrants, substitutes, buyers and suppliers. What is the model usually called?
A company's net profit margin was 12% on revenue of J$750 million. What was its net profit in J$ millions?
What word describes the people and groups with an interest in a firm's strategy, such as owners, staff, customers and regulators?
What term describes a strategy that develops from actions and decisions over time, rather than from the formal plan?
What term describes the ongoing work of collecting and studying information about outside trends that may affect a business?
A firm's market share fell from 18% to 15%. By how many percentage points did it fall?
What term names a planned step to bring results back on track when monitoring shows a gap?
A manufacturer's sales were J$1.2 billion in a market worth J$10 billion. What is its market share as a percentage?

essays.stem: A food manufacturer has approved a five-year strategy with four strategic objectives. Plan the system you would set up to monitor progress against the strategy.
essays.modelAnswer: I would start by linking each strategic objective to two or three KPIs, mixing lagging measures such as revenue growth and market share with leading measures such as new product trials, on-time delivery and staff skills. Each KPI would have a clear definition, a baseline, a yearly target and a named owner, so there is no argument about what is measured or who answers for it. I would set where the data come from and how often: sales and production figures monthly, customer surveys every quarter, and market share and the environmental scan twice a year. The data would be checked for accuracy before use. Results would go on a one-page dashboard with trends and red, amber and green ratings, reported to the management team monthly and to the board quarterly. When a KPI turns amber or red, the owner would explain the cause and propose corrective action. A strategic risk register would be reviewed at the same time. Finally, a full review each year would ask whether the objectives themselves still fit.
markingPoints: Links each objective to a small set of leading and lagging KPIs
Gives KPIs definitions, baselines, targets and owners
Sets data sources, frequency and accuracy checks
Describes reporting with a dashboard and action on red or amber results
Includes risk review and a yearly review of the direction itself

essays.stem: Explain how you would carry out a PESTLE scan for a Jamaican hotel group as part of a strategy review, and how you would use the results.
essays.modelAnswer: I would gather a small team from sales, finance, operations and human resources and agree a time frame, such as the next three years. For each PESTLE heading we would list the trends that could affect the group. Political: government tourism policy and airlift agreements. Economic: visitor arrivals, exchange rates, interest rates and the cost of energy. Social: changing guest tastes, such as demand for local experiences, and the supply of skilled staff. Technological: online booking platforms, mobile check-in and data security. Legal: employment law, the data protection law and licensing. Environmental: hurricanes, coastal erosion and pressure to save water and energy. We would use reliable sources such as official statistics, industry bodies and our own booking data. Then we would rate each factor by its likely effect and how certain it is, and pick the few that matter most. These would feed into an updated SWOT, the strategic risk register and, where needed, scenarios, so the board can decide whether the objectives or the plans should change.
markingPoints: Sets up a team and a time frame for the scan
Gives relevant examples under each PESTLE heading
Uses reliable sources of information
Rates the factors and picks the most important
Feeds the results into SWOT, risks or scenarios and the board's decisions

essays.stem: A distributor's strategy set these targets for year two: sales J$1.5 billion, gross margin 35% and customer satisfaction 85%. The results were sales J$1.2 billion, gross margin 30% and customer satisfaction 88%. Evaluate the performance, showing your working, and recommend what the managers should do.
essays.modelAnswer: Sales reached J$1.2 billion ÷ J$1.5 billion = 80% of target. The target gross profit was 35% × J$1.5 billion = J$525 million, but the actual gross profit was 30% × J$1.2 billion = J$360 million, a shortfall of J$165 million. If the 35% margin had been kept on the actual sales, gross profit would have been J$420 million, so J$105 million of the shortfall comes from lower sales and J$60 million from the lower margin. Customer satisfaction beat its target, which suggests the service strategy is working and customers are loyal. The managers should find out why sales and margin fell: perhaps heavy discounting to win customers, higher import costs or the exchange rate, or a lost market. I would recommend analysing sales and margin by product and customer, reviewing pricing and discount controls, and checking purchase costs. If the market has changed for good, the sales target and plans should be revised with the board's approval. The strong satisfaction score can be used to grow sales with existing customers.
markingPoints: Calculates sales at 80% of target
Calculates target gross profit J$525 million, actual J$360 million and the J$165 million shortfall
Splits the shortfall into volume (J$105 million) and margin (J$60 million), or explains both causes
Notes the satisfaction result and what it suggests
Recommends investigation of causes and justified actions, including possible revision of targets

essays.stem: A review shows that one of a company's strategic objectives is now unlikely to be met because the market has changed. Explain how the managers should decide whether to persist, adjust the plans or change the direction.
essays.modelAnswer: First, the managers should be sure of the facts: check that the data are accurate and find out whether the change in the market is short-term or lasting. They should then review the assumptions the strategy was built on and see which no longer hold. Next, they should set out the options: persist with stronger effort, adjust the plans or targets while keeping the objective, or change the objective and direction. Each option should be tested against clear criteria: fit with the vision and values, likely costs and returns, risks, the firm's capabilities and resources, and the effect on customers, staff and owners. Scenario analysis can show how each option performs if the market improves or worsens. Persisting suits a short-term dip; adjusting suits a slower but still valid path; changing direction is justified only when the evidence shows the old objective no longer fits. The managers should consult key stakeholders and present a reasoned recommendation to the board, which approves any change in direction. The decision and its reasons should be recorded and communicated.
markingPoints: Checks the data and whether the change is short-term or lasting
Reviews the assumptions behind the strategy
Sets out the three options and tests them against clear criteria
Explains when each option suits
Consults, gets board approval and records and communicates the decision

essays.stem: After a strategy review, a company will close its retail counters and move its customers to online and telephone service. Plan how you would communicate this change in direction to staff and other stakeholders.
essays.modelAnswer: I would first list the stakeholders and what each needs to know: counter staff, other staff, customers, suppliers, the board and, where relevant, unions and regulators. Staff directly affected should hear first, in person from senior managers, not from the media or rumours. I would explain why the change is being made, using the review's evidence about how customers now buy, what will happen, when, and what it means for them, including retraining or new roles and how employment law and agreements will be followed. Questions should be answered honestly, and a named contact should handle concerns. Next, I would brief all staff and give team leaders key messages so they can answer questions consistently. Customers would be told in good time through several channels, such as letters, text messages, the website and signs at the counters, with clear help for those less able to use online service. Suppliers and partners would be told what changes for them. I would check understanding through feedback and repeat the key messages as the change rolls out.
markingPoints: Identifies stakeholders and what each needs to know
Tells affected staff first, in person, with reasons and support
Prepares consistent messages for team leaders
Uses suitable channels for customers, with help for those who need it
Seeks feedback and keeps communicating through the change

essays.stem: Explain what strategic drift is, why it happens, and how regular monitoring and review can prevent it. Use a Jamaican business example.
essays.modelAnswer: Strategic drift happens when a firm's strategy slowly stops fitting its environment because the firm keeps doing what worked in the past while customers, technology or competitors move on. Results fall gradually, so managers may not notice until the firm is in trouble. For example, a family-owned taxi company in Kingston might keep relying on phone bookings and street pick-ups while customers move to ride-hailing apps, and lose most of its younger customers before it reacts. Drift happens because of past success, comfortable habits, a narrow view of the market, managers who do not hear bad news, and plans that measure only internal activity. Regular monitoring helps by tracking leading indicators such as customer numbers by age group, booking channels and market share, not just profit. Environmental scanning and listening to front-line staff and customers show changes early. An honest annual review that tests the strategy's assumptions, uses outside views and compares the firm with rivals forces managers to ask whether the direction still fits and to adjust in time.
markingPoints: Defines strategic drift accurately
Gives a relevant Jamaican example
Explains why drift happens
Explains how monitoring of leading indicators and scanning prevent it
Explains the role of an honest review that tests assumptions

essays.stem: Describe the structure and content of a strategy review report to a company's board, and explain how you would make it useful for decision making.
essays.modelAnswer: The report would start with a one-page executive summary giving the main findings and the decisions the board is asked to make. The next section would show progress against each strategic objective, using a dashboard of KPIs with targets, actual results and trends, and a short explanation of the causes of any gaps. A section on the environment would summarise the key changes from the PESTLE scan and competitor review, and what they mean for the firm. The report would then cover the main strategic risks, with any changes in their ratings. The recommendations section would set out options, the preferred option and why, with costs, benefits, risks and a timetable. Detailed data would go in appendices. To make it useful, I would keep it short and clear, use charts rather than long tables, separate facts from opinions, state assumptions, and make sure every figure is checked. I would send it in good time before the meeting so members can read it and prepare questions.
markingPoints: Includes an executive summary with decisions sought
Reports progress on objectives with KPIs and causes of gaps
Covers environmental changes and strategic risks
Gives options and justified recommendations with costs and timing
Explains how to make it clear, accurate and timely

essays.stem: Compare three ways a company can gather stakeholder views as part of reviewing its strategic direction, and recommend how to combine them.
essays.modelAnswer: A customer survey reaches many people at low cost and gives figures that can be tracked over time, such as satisfaction and likelihood to recommend. Its weakness is that it gives little depth and depends on good sampling and question design. Focus groups or interviews with key customers, staff and partners give rich reasons and ideas, and can test new directions, but they reach few people, take time and depend on a skilled facilitator. Staff workshops draw on front-line knowledge of problems and competitors and build commitment to any changes, but staff may hold back if they fear blame, so a safe and respectful setting is needed. Other sources include feedback from regulators, suppliers and community groups. I would recommend combining them: use the survey to measure how widely views are held, interviews and focus groups to understand why, and staff workshops to test whether proposed changes are practical. The findings should be compared, summarised honestly and fed into the review report, and stakeholders should be told how their views were used.
markingPoints: Explains the strengths and limits of a survey
Explains the strengths and limits of interviews or focus groups
Explains the strengths and limits of staff workshops
Recommends a sensible combination with reasons
Feeds findings into the review and reports back to stakeholders

essays.stem: A long-established courier firm in Jamaica is losing small-business customers to a new app-based delivery service. Evaluate the firm's options and recommend a response for its strategy review.
essays.modelAnswer: The firm should first understand why customers are moving: price, speed, tracking, ease of booking on a phone, or all of these. It can then weigh its options. It could compete on price, but this would cut margins and the new rival may be better funded, so a price war is risky. It could improve its own service with online booking, tracking and faster pick-up; this costs money but builds on its strengths of reliability, trained staff and island-wide coverage. It could focus on segments the app serves poorly, such as large or valuable parcels, contracts for regular business customers and rural deliveries. It could also partner with or buy a technology provider to move faster. I would recommend a mix: invest in online booking and tracking within a set budget, and target business customers who value reliability with contract packages, while monitoring market share, customer numbers and margins each month. This uses the firm's strengths, reduces the risk of a price war and can be adjusted as results come in.
markingPoints: Analyses why customers are leaving
Evaluates competing on price and its risks
Evaluates improving service, focusing on segments, or partnering
Makes a justified recommendation that uses the firm's strengths
Includes monitoring measures to check the response

essays.stem: After a strategy review, the board of a manufacturing company changes two of its strategic objectives. Explain how managers should realign operational plans, budgets and people with the revised direction.
essays.modelAnswer: Managers should start by translating the revised objectives into clear priorities and KPIs, so that every unit understands what has changed and why. Each department should then review its operational plan and remove, change or add activities, making sure that each unit target links to a strategic objective. Budgets should be revised so that money follows the new priorities: funds may move from products being phased out to new lines, equipment or marketing, with the board approving any major change. People must also be aligned. Managers should check whether staff have the skills needed, plan training or recruitment, and update job roles and individual performance targets. Systems such as reporting, the dashboard and the risk register should be updated to track the new KPIs. Throughout, managers should communicate openly and involve team leaders, because they turn the new direction into daily work. Finally, an early check after three months should confirm that plans, budgets and people are moving in the new direction, with corrective action where they are not.
markingPoints: Turns the revised objectives into priorities and KPIs
Revises unit plans so that targets link to objectives
Moves budgets to the new priorities with proper approval
Aligns skills, roles and individual targets, and updates reporting systems
Communicates, involves team leaders and checks progress early

practical1.title: Strategy monitoring review and report
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group a made-up case pack for a Jamaican company, such as a food distributor or a hotel group. It includes the company's vision, three strategic objectives with KPIs and targets, two years of results, a short market report and notes on competitors. As a group, carry out a strategy review and write a review report of three to four pages for the board. Each member has a named role: performance analyst (builds a spreadsheet comparing results with targets, works out percentages and gaps, and checks every figure twice); environment analyst (completes a PESTLE scan and picks the three most important factors); competitor analyst (updates the SWOT using the market report and competitor notes); risk analyst (updates a strategic risk register with at least five risks, ratings and owners); and report editor (writes the executive summary and recommendations and puts the report together). In a group of four, the report editor also completes the SWOT. Every member writes the section for their role, and the group agrees the recommendations together.
materials: Computers with word processing and spreadsheet software
PESTLE, SWOT, risk register and report templates
Printer, paper, flipchart paper and markers
photos: The performance spreadsheet on screen, with targets, results and gaps
The PESTLE scan with the top three factors marked
The finished report, open at the executive summary and recommendations
checklist: Took a named role and completed their section of the report
Percentages and gaps are calculated correctly and were checked twice
PESTLE and SWOT points are relevant to the case and are not just listed but rated
Risks have ratings, owners and controls
Recommendations follow from the evidence and say whether to persist, adjust or change direction
The report is clear, well organised and suitable for a board
safety: Treat the case pack as confidential company information; return it to the assessor
Use only made-up company and staff names
Respect each member's analysis and share the workload fairly
Take a short screen break each hour

practical2.title: Board strategy review meeting role play
practical2.brief: Using a made-up case from the assessor (a Jamaican company whose results have fallen behind its strategy, with a one-page dashboard and a short environmental update), your group holds a 45-minute board strategy review meeting and then produces its records. Each member has a named role: board chair (prepares the agenda, runs the meeting fairly and keeps time); strategy manager (presents the progress dashboard and the main gaps in a short slide presentation of no more than six slides); finance director (presents the financial effect of the gaps and of the options, using figures checked twice); operations director (explains the causes on the ground and what each option would mean for staff and customers); and company secretary (records the minutes, decisions and actions). In a group of four, the chair also takes the minutes, with help from the finance director. The meeting must consider at least three options (persist, adjust or change direction), agree a decision with reasons, and agree how the change will be communicated. After the meeting, the group writes the minutes, an action list with owners and dates, and a one-page communication plan for staff and customers. Every member writes or checks part of these documents.
materials: Case pack, dashboard and environmental update from the assessor
Computer and projector or screen for the slides
Agenda, minutes, action list and communication plan templates
photos: The agenda and the strategy manager's slides
The meeting in progress (faces only if all agree)
The options compared on a flipchart or slide
The minutes with the decision and its reasons
The action list and the communication plan
checklist: Took a named role and prepared for it
Presented or contributed clearly, using evidence and accurate figures
Options were compared against clear criteria before deciding
The decision and its reasons are recorded accurately in the minutes
Actions have owners and dates, and the communication plan names the audiences and channels
Behaved professionally and respected other members' views
safety: Keep the case and the minutes confidential; return all papers to the assessor
Challenge ideas, not people, during the meeting
Use made-up names only and keep personal opinions about real firms out of the role play
Share the writing fairly and take a short break after the meeting
